paragraphs: Categorical features describe groups or labels, while many machine learning models require numerical inputs. Encoders provide that translation, and choosing one is an important part of building a classifier. This paper examines how to compare encoders for binary classification, where the prediction has two possible outcomes, through a substantially broader benchmark than earlier studies.

The benchmark evaluates 32 encoder configurations drawn from different families, across 36 combinations of experimental factors and 50 datasets. These dimensions matter together: an encoder comparison depends on which methods enter the comparison, the conditions under which they are evaluated, and the data used to assess them. The study also examines how individual results are combined into overall conclusions.

The central finding is that dataset selection, experimental factors, and aggregation strategies strongly influence the benchmark's conclusions. That makes the evaluation procedure itself a substantive part of the result. The contribution is a broad empirical comparison that shows why encoder recommendations must be interpreted in the context of the choices used to produce them.
neurips-2023-a-benchmark-of-categorical-.tldr: A broad categorical-encoder benchmark shows that datasets, experimental conditions, and result aggregation strongly shape comparison outcomes.

paragraphs: Concept-based explanations try to describe a neural network's decisions through understandable visual patterns in its internal activations. They typically involve two tasks: finding those concepts and estimating how much each contributes to a prediction. This paper provides a shared theoretical framework for methods that implement these tasks in different ways.

The framework treats concept extraction as dictionary learning: finding a collection of patterns that can represent the network's activations. It treats concept importance as attribution, connecting the question of which concepts matter to established ways of assigning credit for predictions. These connections support new evaluation metrics, extensions using modern attribution techniques, and theoretical guarantees about the optimality of such methods.

The authors also use the framework to investigate how to identify groups of examples that a model classifies through similar strategies. They introduce strategic cluster graphs to visualize these shared approaches and provide visualizations for every ImageNet class through Lens. The contribution therefore joins methodological comparison with a way to inspect recurring decision patterns across examples.
neurips-2023-a-holistic-approach-to-unif.tldr: A unified framework connects concept extraction to dictionary learning and concept importance to attribution, supporting evaluation and visualization of model strategies.

paragraphs: Algorithmic programming requires both choosing a suitable algorithm and implementing it correctly. ALGO addresses these challenges by asking a language model to generate a reference program, or oracle, that exhaustively enumerates combinations of relevant variables. This oracle supplies a reference against which proposed solutions can be checked.

The framework uses the generated oracle to guide a search through possible algorithms and verify candidate programs. Its design can accommodate different search strategies and existing code generation models. The important separation is between producing a reference answer through exhaustive enumeration and searching for an algorithmic solution that agrees with that reference.

In the study, generated oracles were correct in 88% of cases, so the reference-generation step itself was imperfect. Nevertheless, ALGO produced substantial empirical gains: one-submission pass rates were eight times those of Codex and 2.6 times those of CodeT on CodeContests. It also achieved a 1.3-fold pass-rate improvement over ChatGPT Code Interpreter on unseen problems. These findings support generated verification as a useful aid to algorithm synthesis, while retaining the stated qualification about oracle correctness.
neurips-2023-algo-synthesizing-algorithm.tldr: ALGO uses language-model-generated exhaustive reference programs to guide algorithm synthesis and improve empirical programming pass rates.

paragraphs: A clinical prediction model can lose accuracy when the patients or conditions it encounters differ from its training data. Existing approaches to this domain shift often assume that domain labels are available and train one model across all domains. The paper argues that healthcare data can instead contain numerous hidden patient groups with distinct clinical characteristics.

SLGD addresses this setting through an iterative self-learning process. It discovers separate domains within the data and trains a personalized classifier for each discovered domain. Domain discovery and classifier training are therefore parts of the same framework. This targets both the absence of known domain categories and the potential inadequacy of a single classifier for clinically different groups.

The authors evaluate generalization under spatial and temporal distribution shifts using the public eICU and MIMIC-IV electronic health record datasets. They report improvements of up to 11% in AUPRC over the best baseline. This is an empirical result for the evaluated shifts, supporting the usefulness of discovering latent domains and fitting classifiers tailored to them.
neurips-2023-an-iterative-self-learning-.tldr: SLGD iteratively discovers hidden patient domains and trains domain-specific classifiers, improving generalization across evaluated healthcare data shifts.

paragraphs: Understanding an AI system that plans and acts requires more than knowing whether it succeeded on a particular task. Users also need to understand which capabilities it has, the conditions needed to use them, and their possible effects. This paper studies how to learn such descriptions when the system is a black box and outcomes are stochastic.

The proposed approach actively interacts with the system to learn an interpretable probabilistic model of its capabilities. Active learning makes interaction part of the assessment process, while the probabilistic representation captures the possibility of different outcomes. The resulting model describes both what actions can accomplish and what requirements govern their execution.

The theoretical analysis identifies conditions under which learning converges to the correct model of the agent. That guarantee is conditional on those identified conditions. Experiments with different agents and simulated scenarios show sample-efficient capability descriptions and generalization from few examples. Together, the results support automated capability assessment through interaction, connecting observed behavior to a description users can interpret.
neurips-2023-autonomous-capability-asses.tldr: An active-learning approach builds interpretable probabilistic descriptions of black-box agents' capabilities, with conditional convergence guarantees and sample-efficient empirical results.

paragraphs: Generating images does not by itself provide the detailed labels needed to train perception systems. DatasetDM extends a pretrained diffusion model so that it produces synthetic images together with annotations such as segmentation masks and depth. The aim is to reduce the collection and labeling effort associated with large training datasets.

Its central component is a decoder that turns the diffusion model's internal latent representation into perception annotations. Training this decoder requires around 100 manually labeled images, described as less than 1% of the labeled images. Once trained, the system can keep generating annotated examples for downstream models, including semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and depth estimation.

The authors report state-of-the-art results in semantic and instance segmentation, as well as zero-shot segmentation. They also report more efficient and robust domain generalization than using real data in their evaluation. Beyond individual prediction tasks, the approach supports combinations of tasks such as image editing. The main contribution is making generated visual content useful as labeled training material through information already present inside a diffusion model.
neurips-2023-datasetdm-synthesizing-data.tldr: DatasetDM decodes diffusion-model representations into perception labels, enabling large synthetic training datasets from a small manually annotated starting set.

paragraphs: An embodied agent must choose actions that fit its surroundings, work across object types, and avoid actions that are invalid in the current situation. Egocentric Planning combines symbolic planning with an object-oriented model of decision-making under partial observability. It also uses existing visual perception and natural language processing models to support task execution.

The symbolic component describes the preconditions and effects of actions: what must hold before an action and what it can change. The approach also needs information about which object types reveal information about others. These requirements make its dependence on reliable perception and specified or learned symbolic knowledge explicit.

On ALFRED, a simulated benchmark for domestic tasks, the approach achieves a 36.07% unseen success rate and won the associated challenge at the CVPR Embodied AI workshop. The authors argue that it can scale to new tasks beyond ALFRED when those tasks are solvable using available skills. Its contribution is a hybrid planning baseline for studying generalization and robustness, including tasks that require long action sequences.
neurips-2023-egocentric-planning-for-sca.tldr: Egocentric Planning combines symbolic action knowledge and object-oriented decision-making to perform embodied tasks, achieving 36.07% unseen success on ALFRED.

paragraphs: Federated zeroth-order optimization combines distributed learning with optimization that approximates gradient information. Although FedZO had performed well on tasks such as black-box attacks and softmax regression, its theoretical understanding lagged behind its practical use. This paper studies both generalization, meaning performance beyond the training data, and convergence, meaning progress toward an optimization solution.

The analysis develops an on-average model stability technique, examining how changes in training data affect the learned model. Under Lipschitz continuity and smoothness conditions, it establishes the first generalization error bound for FedZO. The authors then refine the generalization and optimization bounds by replacing a bounded-gradient assumption with heavy-tailed gradient noise and using a second-order Taylor expansion in the gradient approximation.

A new decomposition of the error extends the analysis to asynchronous operation. The contribution is therefore a more complete theoretical account of FedZO across these settings. The results fill a missing generalization guarantee and sharpen the characterization of convergence; they describe the algorithm's behavior under the stated mathematical conditions.
neurips-2023-fine-grained-theoretical-an.tldr: A stability-based analysis establishes conditional generalization guarantees and sharper optimization bounds for FedZO, including asynchronous operation.

paragraphs: Split inference divides neural-network computation between an edge device and the cloud to address device constraints and support privacy. However, attackers may still reconstruct a user's private prediction input. The paper studies this vulnerability, focusing on weaknesses in attacks that either make limited use of public data or depend heavily on auxiliary data quantity and similarity.

GLASS uses a generative adversarial network and a search through its latent space to reconstruct private inputs. Advanced StyleGAN models supply prior knowledge learned from public data. This makes the generator's learned representation central to the attack. The authors also introduce GLASS++, a variant designed to improve the stability of reconstruction.

The authors describe this as the first GAN-based reconstruction attack against split inference. Evaluations across different network split points and adversary setups show state-of-the-art attack performance. They also examine seven defense mechanisms and show that the method can reveal private information in their presence. The findings demonstrate that the privacy of split computation must be assessed against attacks able to exploit strong generative prior knowledge.
neurips-2023-gan-you-see-me-enhanced-dat.tldr: GLASS uses StyleGAN-based latent-space search to strengthen reconstruction attacks against split inference, including in evaluations with seven defenses.

paragraphs: A partially observed point cloud can support several plausible interpretations of an object's pose. This paper addresses that ambiguity by treating category-level pose estimation as conditional generation. A score-based diffusion model samples candidate poses, allowing the method to represent multiple hypotheses before producing its final estimate.

The candidates are combined in two stages. First, likelihood estimates identify and remove outliers. Then the remaining candidates are averaged. Because likelihood estimation through the original diffusion model involves costly integration, the authors distill an energy-based model from it to provide end-to-end likelihood estimation. This connects the generation and selection of pose hypotheses within the overall approach.

On REAL275, the method reports state-of-the-art performance, exceeding 50% on the strict 5-degree, 2-centimeter metric and 60% on the 5-degree, 5-centimeter metric. It also shows strong generalization to new categories without fine-tuning. Adaptation to pose tracking produces results comparable to state-of-the-art baselines. These findings support generating and filtering multiple poses as a useful response to ambiguity in incomplete observations.
neurips-2023-generative-category-level-o.tldr: A diffusion-based pose estimator samples multiple hypotheses, filters them by likelihood, and averages the survivors to handle incomplete object observations.

paragraphs: Imitation learning aims to teach an agent from expert demonstrations, but transferring that behavior to unfamiliar environments remains difficult. Adaptive Return-conditioned Policy, or ARP, uses natural language task descriptions and pretrained multimodal encoders to provide an additional training signal. It connects what the agent sees with the task it is meant to accomplish.

The method measures similarity between visual observations and language instructions in a shared embedding space, such as CLIP's. It uses that similarity as a reward and attaches these rewards to expert demonstrations. A return-conditioned policy then learns from the labeled demonstrations. Because the visual-language reward supplies a signal at each timestep, it provides task-related guidance throughout the demonstrated behavior.

The authors report that this approach mitigates goal misgeneralization and generalizes better than existing text-conditioned policies, including when instructions are unseen. They also introduce a way to fine-tune the multimodal encoder, improving reward quality and further increasing performance. The contribution is to turn pretrained visual-language alignment into adaptive reward information for learning from demonstrations.
neurips-2023-guide-your-agent-with-adapt.tldr: ARP converts visual-language similarity into rewards for expert demonstrations, improving reported imitation-learning generalization to unseen instructions and environments.

paragraphs: Mixed linear regression assumes that each observation comes from one of several unknown linear models. The difficulty increases when some models contribute many more observations than others. This paper introduces Mix-IRLS to address that imbalance, while also aiming to perform well when the groups have similar sizes.

Mix-IRLS recovers the component models sequentially using robust regression tools. This changes the organization of the problem from estimating all models simultaneously to recovering them one after another. The authors describe the resulting algorithm as simple and fast, and derive a recovery guarantee that highlights its advantage for imbalanced mixtures.

The empirical evaluation finds strong performance across balanced and imbalanced mixtures. It also reports success in settings with few samples, outliers, or an unknown number of component models, where competing approaches fail in the evaluated cases. On several real-world datasets, Mix-IRLS outperforms competing methods, sometimes by a large margin. The combination of empirical results and a recovery guarantee supports sequential robust regression as a useful approach to mixture estimation.
neurips-2023-imbalanced-mixed-linear-reg.tldr: Mix-IRLS sequentially recovers linear models using robust regression, with strong empirical performance and a recovery guarantee highlighting imbalanced mixtures.

paragraphs: Multimodal systems combine information from different kinds of inputs. Learning their interactions commonly assumes that the combinations needed at inference also appear during training. This paper studies the more demanding case in which a system must work with combinations of modalities it has never encountered together.

The proposed method projects the multidimensional features of each modality into a common representation while preserving rich information. It then combines the available representations by summation. This shared format lets information from different modalities accumulate through the same operation, providing a mechanism for handling combinations beyond those used during training.

The training procedure also uses pseudo-supervision that indicates the reliability of a modality's prediction. This is intended to reduce overfitting to combinations that are less informative for the task. Evaluations cover multimodal video classification, robot state regression, and multimedia retrieval, demonstrating effectiveness across different tasks and input types. The contribution is both a formulation of unseen modality interaction and an initial method that learns representations designed to combine flexibly.
neurips-2023-learning-unseen-modality-in.tldr: A shared representation and reliability-based training enable multimodal models to handle input combinations absent from training.

paragraphs: Lung registration aligns scans of the same patient taken at different breathing stages. Large breathing-related motion makes this challenging, and existing public resources have limitations for training and comparing modern methods. Some contain too few examples or mostly small motions; a large vessel point-cloud dataset lacks training correspondences and publicly available matching CT scans.

Lung250M-4B brings image-based and point-based registration into a combined benchmark. The authors curate 248 public CT scans from 124 patients across multiple centers, pairing inhalation and exhalation scans with large motion. They process the scans for sufficient homogeneity and generate vessel point clouds that also cover regions deeper inside the lungs.

For supervised training, the dataset includes vein and artery segmentations and several thousand image-derived keypoint correspondences per pair. Validation pairs include manually annotated landmarks. The authors also evaluate several image and point-cloud registration methods as initial baselines. The central contribution is a shared data resource that supports supervised learning and more direct comparison of approaches operating on different representations of lung anatomy.
neurips-2023-lung250m-4b-a-combined-3d-d.tldr: Lung250M-4B combines paired lung CT scans, vessel point clouds, and correspondence annotations to support training and comparison of registration methods.

paragraphs: Document retrieval often uses vector representations to find documents similar to a query quickly. Deep retrieval models offer stronger model quality, but their serving latency and difficulties supporting document updates can hinder deployment. Model-enhanced Vector Index, or MEVI, aims to combine the learning advantages of deep generative retrieval with efficient vector search.

MEVI connects a sequence-to-sequence retrieval model and an embedding-based model through a residual quantization codebook. A twin-tower representation model supplies the embeddings. During retrieval, the generative component first predicts semantic identifiers for candidate virtual clusters in a small number of steps. Vector search then finds relevant documents within those candidate clusters.

This two-stage process avoids spending many sequential decoding steps on complete, unique document identifiers. Generation narrows the search, and adapted embeddings perform the detailed comparison. Experiments on MSMARCO Passage and Natural Questions show improved retrieval performance with serving latency comparable to dense retrieval systems. The reported result supports integrating learned cluster selection into a vector index while retaining practical search speed.
neurips-2023-model-enhanced-vector-index.tldr: MEVI generates candidate document clusters and searches them with embeddings, improving retrieval performance at latency comparable to dense retrieval.

paragraphs: Exploration in reinforcement learning determines which experiences an agent collects while searching for a good policy. This paper starts from an information-theoretic question: how many samples does a particular problem require to identify a nearly optimal policy? Such instance-specific lower bounds can inform exploration, but deriving them and the corresponding optimal strategy requires a system model and a difficult optimization.

The authors derive an approximation to this lower bound that depends only on quantities obtainable through model-free methods. This creates a connection between a theoretically motivated sample requirement and exploration that does not rely on estimating the system model. They use the approximation to construct an exploration strategy based on an ensemble.

The resulting strategy applies to both tabular and continuous Markov decision processes. Numerical experiments show that it identifies efficient policies faster than state-of-the-art exploration approaches in the evaluated settings. The contribution is a model-free route to exploration guided by an approximation of instance-specific information requirements, with empirical evidence that this guidance accelerates policy discovery.
neurips-2023-model-free-active-explorati.tldr: An ensemble-based exploration strategy uses a model-free approximation of information-theoretic sample requirements to accelerate empirical policy discovery.

paragraphs: In online prediction, a learner repeatedly draws on expert advice about binary events. This paper allows the learner to select several experts each round, while the experts may misreport their beliefs to increase their influence. The challenge is to obtain good predictions without rewarding strategic dishonesty.

The desired algorithms have two properties. Incentive compatibility makes truthful reporting advantageous for experts. No-regret performance means that cumulative regret grows sublinearly compared with the best fixed group of the same size, evaluated using its true beliefs and chosen in hindsight. The paper considers both additive group utility and submodular utility, which captures diminishing returns from adding experts.

Earlier results addressed selecting a single expert. The authors show that a simple reduction of group selection to that case is neither efficient nor effective. They instead construct algorithms that exploit the structure of the utility functions to achieve truthful incentives and no-regret performance together. The framework is relevant to forecasting competitions where a learner needs both to combine predictions and to rank forecasters by performance.
neurips-2023-no-regret-online-prediction.tldr: Structure-aware algorithms select groups of strategic experts while encouraging truthful reports and achieving sublinear regret.

paragraphs: Input gradients describe how a neural network's output changes as its input changes, making them useful for visual explanations and robustness analysis. In conventional networks, gradient-based saliency maps can be noisy. This paper studies 1-Lipschitz networks trained with the dual loss of an optimal transport problem and finds that their gradients provide particularly useful explanations.

The authors prove that the gradient encodes both the direction of a transport plan and the direction toward the nearest adversarial attack. This gives the gradient a geometric meaning tied to movement between classes. Following it toward the decision boundary can therefore be interpreted as a counterfactual explanation showing how an input is transported from one class toward another.

The reported saliency maps concentrate on essential image regions with little noise and outperform state-of-the-art explanation approaches across the evaluated models and metrics. The authors also establish strong alignment with human explanations on ImageNet and demonstrate scaling to large models and problems. The contribution connects the training objective, classification behavior, and explanatory gradient within networks already known for certified robustness.
neurips-2023-on-the-explainable-properti.tldr: Optimal-transport training gives 1-Lipschitz networks informative gradients, connecting clear saliency maps to transport directions and counterfactual explanations.

paragraphs: Private learning traditionally produces a hypothesis from labeled training data while protecting the training set. For some concept classes, privacy greatly increases the required sample size or makes traditional private learning impossible. This paper studies a different interface: answering an ongoing stream of classification queries while protecting both the training data and the queries themselves.

The authors call this private everlasting prediction. Queries may be chosen adaptively, and the predictor changes the hypothesis it uses over time. They observe that this updating cannot depend solely on the original training set. The framework therefore treats privacy and continued prediction as an ongoing process rather than a single release of a learned hypothesis.

The paper gives a generic construction in the PAC model for every concept class with finite VC dimension. Its initial labeled sample requirement is quadratic in that dimension, up to polylogarithmic factors. The construction includes threshold functions over infinite domains, where traditional private learning is impossible. This establishes that changing the learning interface to an enduring prediction service enables a broader private prediction result.
neurips-2023-private-everlasting-predict.tldr: Private everlasting prediction answers continuing adaptive queries while protecting training data and queries, covering every finite-VC-dimension concept class in the PAC model.

paragraphs: Transformer attention becomes memory-intensive as context grows. Ways of extending context can restrict access to earlier tokens or introduce a separate retrieval system whose choices may not fit the model's attention. This paper introduces landmark attention to retain flexible access to the full context while selecting only relevant blocks for retrieval.

Each input block receives a landmark token that represents it. The model learns to use attention over these landmarks to select relevant blocks, bringing retrieval into the attention mechanism itself. The approach also integrates with specialized data structures and the system's memory hierarchy, enabling support for arbitrarily long contexts while preserving access across the context.

The authors report performance comparable to Transformer-XL while retrieving substantially fewer tokens per step. They also fine-tune LLaMA 7B and demonstrate context capacity beyond 32,000 tokens. These experiments provide a concrete demonstration of extended context, alongside the broader architectural support for arbitrary lengths. The contribution is an attention-compatible way to locate useful information across a large context without retrieving all of it at every step.
neurips-2023-random-access-infinite-cont.tldr: Landmark attention retrieves context blocks through learned attention, preserving flexible access and extending demonstrated LLaMA 7B context beyond 32,000 tokens.

paragraphs: Recommendation training data are affected by selection bias: the ratings collected do not represent an unbiased view of all possible ratings. Methods that adjust for observed user and item features can still miss hidden confounding. This paper analyzes how such hidden influences can undermine attempts to learn unbiased recommendations.

The theoretical analysis shows possible failures of propensity-based methods, multi-task learning, and bi-level optimization when hidden confounding is present. It also identifies a restriction of sensitivity-based approaches: their worst-case protection is valid only when the true propensity lies within a finite bound around the nominal estimate. These findings motivate adding an unbiased source of information.

The proposed unified multi-task approach uses a small number of unbiased ratings to calibrate both nominal propensities and nominal error imputations learned from biased data. It therefore links information about observation likelihood and estimated errors through the same calibration resource. Experiments on three public benchmark datasets, including a large fully exposed industrial dataset, support the effectiveness of this approach in removing hidden confounding in the evaluated recommendation settings.
neurips-2023-removing-hidden-confounding.tldr: A unified multi-task recommender uses a few unbiased ratings to calibrate bias corrections and address hidden confounding.

paragraphs: Sparse deep learning has been used for uncertainty estimation, variable selection, and network compression, but much of its theory assumes independent observations. Time series violate that assumption because observations depend on one another. This paper develops a theoretical treatment of sparse deep learning for dependent data, focusing on recurrent neural networks.

Under appropriate assumptions, the authors show that sparse recurrent networks can be estimated consistently and that their predictions become normally distributed asymptotically. These properties provide a basis for correctly quantifying prediction uncertainty in the studied setting. The asymptotic statement concerns behavior as data grow, and its validity depends on the assumptions used in the analysis.

Numerical results show better time-series uncertainty quantification than state-of-the-art methods including conformal prediction. The results also indicate consistent identification of autoregressive order and stronger large-scale model compression than existing methods. The contribution connects sparse modeling to several goals at once: predicting dependent observations, assessing uncertainty, identifying relevant temporal structure, and reducing model size. This combination is relevant where both point predictions and their uncertainty matter.
neurips-2023-sparse-deep-learning-for-ti.tldr: The paper develops conditional statistical guarantees for sparse recurrent networks on dependent data and reports gains in uncertainty quantification and compression.

paragraphs: A universal formula is a parameterized expression of fixed complexity that can approximate any continuous function on a compact set. Some neural-network constructions have this property. This paper investigates which structural ingredients make such expressiveness possible and how weaker forms of expressive power relate to full approximation over a domain.

The authors introduce a hierarchy connecting global approximation with infinite VC dimension, a weaker measure of capacity. They classify several increasingly complex function families. In particular, they define a general family of polynomially-exponentially-algebraic functions and prove that it obeys polynomial constraints, providing a mathematical route to limits on expressiveness.

One consequence is that fixed-size networks with at most one layer of neurons using transcendental activations, such as sine or standard sigmoid, cannot generally approximate functions on arbitrary finite sets. Conversely, the paper gives families, including two-hidden-layer networks, that can approximate functions on arbitrary finite sets but fail across the whole domain. These results distinguish fitting any finite collection of values from having genuine global approximation power.
neurips-2023-structure-of-universal-form.tldr: A hierarchy of expressiveness reveals structural limits and separates arbitrary finite-set approximation from universal approximation across a domain.

paragraphs: Gaussian mixture models have supported many theoretical results in high-dimensional statistics, but applying those results to more general data requires justification. This paper asks when detailed distributional structure can be replaced by the means and covariances of mixture components without changing the relevant asymptotic statistics.

The analysis considers independent samples from a mixture distribution and generalized linear models that apply a function to linear projections of the input. It studies families of estimators obtained either by minimizing empirical risk or by sampling from an associated Gibbs distribution. Looking at the family jointly allows the analysis to address relationships among estimators as well as their individual behavior.

The main result characterizes conditions under which those joint statistics depend, in a weak asymptotic sense, only on component means and covariances. This yields universality results for training and generalization errors, estimator geometry, and correlations. The contribution is a rigorous basis for extending Gaussian-mixture calculations to a broader class of datasets when the required conditions hold, rather than treating the Gaussian assumption as automatically representative.
neurips-2023-universality-laws-for-gauss.tldr: Conditional universality results show when generalized linear estimators' asymptotic behavior depends only on mixture-component means and covariances.

paragraphs: Very wide neural networks can correspond to Gaussian processes, providing a mathematical framework for analyzing their behavior. Much of the existing theory concerns shallow networks or networks of finite depth. This paper extends the analysis to deep equilibrium models, which represent infinite-depth networks with shared weight matrices across layers.

The authors show that a deep equilibrium model converges to a Gaussian process as its layer width tends to infinity. They also establish that this convergence holds when the order of the depth and width limits is exchanged. That property distinguishes the studied equilibrium models from typical infinite-depth multilayer perceptrons, where the same interchangeability is not observed.

For pairwise distinct inputs, the resulting Gaussian vector is non-degenerate. Equivalently, the corresponding kernel matrix has a strictly positive smallest eigenvalue, so the limiting representation does not collapse along a direction across those inputs. These results supply mathematical building blocks for investigating training and generalization in deep equilibrium models. Their stated role is foundational, establishing properties of the limiting model on which further analysis can build.
neurips-2023-wide-neural-networks-as-gau.tldr: Wide deep equilibrium models converge to Gaussian processes with interchangeable depth and width limits and non-degenerate kernels on distinct inputs.
